The growth in Grab's deliveries revenue in FY2025 (which rose to $1,800 million from $1,493 million in 2024) was driven by several factors:

1. **Increased deliveries GMV**: GMV grew 21%, or $2.5 billion, to $14.2 billion in 2025 compared to $11.7 billion in 2024, mainly due to increased consumer demand and platform engagement with technology-led product innovations [Grab, FY2025, p.98].

2. **Supermarket business contribution**: Revenue included an increase of $161 million in contributions from the supermarket business, which includes Everrise, acquired in 2025 [Grab, FY2025, p.98].

3. **Product initiatives and engagement**: Revenue growth was driven by further adoption of key affordability and high-value product initiatives, as well as newer features such as Group Orders and Dine Out, as Grab expanded its product offerings and increased platform engagement, reflected in the growth of MTUs, which rose 17% to 25.4 million [Grab, FY2025, p.98; Grab, FY2025, p.97].

4. **Stable revenue-to-GMV ratio**: Deliveries revenue as a percentage of deliveries GMV remained consistent at 13% in both 2025 and 2024 [Grab, FY2025, p.98].

This revenue growth was partially offset by higher incentives, as partner incentives increased to $620 million (from $482 million in 2024) and consumer incentives increased to $1,004 million (from $829 million in 2024), as Grab continued to drive new user growth and product adoption [Grab, FY2025, p.98; Grab, FY2025, p.97].
